images.title: Cutting the letter A from folded paper
images.purpose: Put the hook's idea in front of the student before any rule is said: a square paper is folded in half, half of the letter A is drawn along the fold, cut out, and the opened paper shows the full letter A.
images.composition: Four panels in one row, each with a caption above it, and a small arrow between neighbouring panels, going from the folded paper to the opened letter.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Four panels in one row. Each panel is a rounded rectangle 300 wide and 360 tall with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline and a white fill, at x 68 to 368, 408 to 708, 748 to 1048 and 1088 to 1388, all at y 230 to 590. Above each panel, centred on it at about y 190, a caption in dark #1F2937 sans-serif (40 px): Step 1, Step 2, Step 3, Step 4. PANEL 1: a square sheet of paper, amber #E69F00, 220 by 220 px, centred in the panel (x 108 to 328, y 300 to 520), with one dashed vertical fold line in grey #6B7280 (4 px dashes) down its exact middle at x 218, running from y 280 to y 540. PANEL 2: the sheet folded in half: a tall amber rectangle 110 by 220 px (x 453 to 563, y 300 to 520) with its folded edge on the right, drawn as a thicker 6 px dark line; on it the left half of a capital letter A, drawn as a teal #0072B2 outline 6 px thick, with its straight side lying on the folded edge. PANEL 3: the same folded rectangle at the same place, now with the half letter A cut out: the half A shape is filled teal #0072B2 and the paper around it is gone, so the half A stands alone with its straight edge on the right. PANEL 4: the opened sheet, an amber square 220 by 220 px, with the full capital letter A in teal #0072B2, about 180 px tall, filling the middle, exactly symmetrical about a faint dashed vertical line in grey #6B7280 at the middle. Between the panels, exactly 3 small arrows pointing right, in reddish purple #CC79A7, one in each 40 px gap at y 410. In all there are exactly 4 panels, 3 arrows and 4 captions. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a letter A that is not symmetrical about the fold
any other letter, number or text in the frame
images.takeaway: A letter can be cut out of folded paper by drawing only half of it along the fold.
images.description: Four steps: a square paper with a dashed fold line, the folded paper with half of the letter A drawn on it, the half A cut out, and the opened paper showing the full letter A.
images.context: Concept image for the hook, Prem and Manu's Birthday Cutouts. It follows the idea of the four pictures in your maths book (fold, draw half, cut, open) and says nothing about which other letters can be cut.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student see that the cut half becomes a whole letter when the paper is opened. Do not say which letters work: that is the question the free-try tool opens.

image_decisions.why: The four pictures of the folded paper and the cut A put the hook question, which letters can be cut out the easy way, in front of the student without giving the answer.
